bib.title: THOUGHTSCULPT: Reasoning with Intermediate Revision and Search

question: Can an inference-time MCTS over LLM thoughts, whose action space includes revising earlier output, beat CoT, Self-Refine and Tree-of-Thoughts on tasks that need continual revision?
hypothesis: Tree search methods limited to the candidates generated at earlier steps (ToT) and linear self-refinement (Self-Refine) are weaker than a search that can revise intermediate nodes.
contributions: ThoughtSculpt: MCTS over thought nodes with thought evaluator, thought generator and decision simulator, where the action space includes revising previous output
Evaluation on Story Outline Improvement, Mini-Crosswords and Constrained Generation (CommonGen-Hard) against CoT, Self-Refine and ToT
Shows the method works with DFS as well as MCTS and needs no training or external feedback

method.summary: Each thought node is a full or partial output. A thought evaluator (LLM) returns numeric score and natural-language feedback (holistic or itemized); a thought generator (LLM) proposes k child nodes conditioned on task, parent and feedback; a decision simulator does MCTS rollouts (UCB1 selection, expansion, single-child simulation to depth d_simulation, backpropagation). The node with the highest average reward is returned. Runs entirely at inference time on GPT-3.5 and GPT-4.
method.task: inference-time reasoning/revision search: story outline improvement, 5x5 mini crosswords, CommonGen-Hard constrained generation (also Game of 24)

datasets.name: WhatsThatBook book descriptions (story outline task)
datasets.size: 500 book descriptions sampled; 400 train / 50 val / 50 test
datasets.split: 400 for training the content evaluator, 50 validation, 50 test outlines
datasets.source: Lin et al., 2023; outlines generated with DOC (Yang et al., 2023) using GPT-3.5
datasets.preprocessing: Three outlines per description: prompted interesting, prompted boring, default. Evaluator data: 400 interesting + 400 non-interesting for fine-tuning, 50+50 validation, 50 test outlines

datasets.name: CommonGen-Hard
datasets.source: Madaan et al. (2023); 20-30 concepts per item, from CommonGen (Lin et al., 2020)

datasets.name: Game of 24
datasets.source: same test set as Yao et al. (2023a)

other.fine_tuning: learning rate 3e-4, weight decay 0.1, 5 epochs; rates interesting outlines 1 and boring 0; hidden from all methods during generation

other.use: swapped in for the evaluator and/or generator in the Table 10 ablation (Constrained Generation)

inference.decoding: UCB1 tree policy for MCTS; DFS variant picks highest-reward child greedily
inference.samples: not stated; single run per method implied, no seeds or significance tests reported
inference.prompting: three prompts per task: TASK_DESCRIPTION, NEW_CANDIDATE, EVALUATE_CURRENT (itemized and/or holistic); see prompts

parameters.crossword_search_steps: 20 (vs 100 in Yao et al.); also run at 100 in Appendix F
parameters.evaluator_score_scale_story: interestingness 1 to 10 (itemized); EVALUATE_CURRENT prompt asks 1 to 100

metrics.name: Average outline interestingness
metrics.definition: output of a fine-tuned Flan-T5 content evaluator on revised outlines (interesting=1, boring=0), reported as a percentage

metrics.name: Mini-crossword success
metrics.definition: proportion of words, letters, and games correctly filled

metrics.name: Concept coverage
metrics.definition: share of the 20-30 required concepts present in the generated sentence

metrics.name: Human preference
metrics.definition: Prolific annotators, 100 pairs of outlines (ThoughtSculpt MCTS vs ToT or Self-Refine), two annotators per pair, GPT-3.5 base

metrics.name: G-Eval interestingness
metrics.definition: G-Eval with a definition prompt of interestingness, scored by GPT-4 or GPT-3.5

eval.protocol: Same base LM and temperature across methods. Story outlines judged by hidden fine-tuned evaluator plus human pairwise preference and G-Eval; coverage also compared by GPT-4 preference. Number of runs and variance not reported.

availability.code: promised upon publication; no URL in text
availability.data: public datasets (WhatsThatBook, CommonGen-Hard, ToT crossword and Game of 24 sets); Flan-T5 open source

prompts.text: NEW_CANDIDATE = TASK_DESCRIPTION + "# Original Outline {outline} # Feedback {feedback} Based on the feedback and the task description, can you make a better story outline by replacing the items suggested by the feedback? Write the outline in this format just like the original outline from [1] to [{num}]"
prompts.where: Appendix A.1 (abridged; full text in the paper)

prompts.text: Which continuous {num_consecutive_lines} outlines items do you think are least interesting? ... Write in this format: Thought Process: ... [reason: ...] [start_index]-[end_index] [interesting level: 1-10] ... Can you provide {num_candidates} proposals?
Evaluate the current board and provide a strategy on how to continue to fill in the blank or correct potential mistakes.

Do you think that the proposed sentence is good enough? Write "no need to improve" if you think 1) the sentence covers all the concepts listed in the instruction; and 2) the sentence describes a common scene in daily life. Otherwise, write "still need to improve" and provide a reason.

results.claim: On story outline improvement with GPT-3.5, ThoughtSculpt with MCTS reaches the highest interestingness, well above ToT.
results.setup: Story Outline Improvement, GPT-3.5 base, depth 3, 3 candidates per node, judged by fine-tuned Flan-T5 evaluator
results.quote: ThoughtSculpt with MCTS demonstrates the highest average interestingness percentage across both GPT-3.5 and GPT-4 with 89.9 and 65.0 respectively
results.note: The quote in the text wraps across lines in the PDF; Table 1 gives ToT 72.1, Self-refine 65.5, CoT 50.1, initial outline 12.0

results.claim: Same task with GPT-4: MCTS 65.0 vs ToT 49.9, Self-refine 27.9 and CoT 28.8, so GPT-4 baselines can fall below GPT-3.5 ones.
results.note: Authors suggest GPT-4 scores lower overall because the evaluator was trained on GPT-3.5 outlines (footnote 1)

results.claim: In the 20-step mini-crossword with GPT-4, MCTS has the highest word success and game success; ToT is worse than Self-refine on words.
results.setup: Mini-crossword, GPT-4, 20 search steps, 3 candidates per node
results.table: Table 2, row THOUGHTSCULPT (MCTS), column GPT4 % word
results.note: Game success 25.0 for MCTS vs 5.0 for ToT and Self-refine; with GPT-3.5 ToT word 19.5 vs MCTS 19.0 and game success 0.0 for both. The text says 'As shown in Table 8' but the main-text table is Table 2

results.claim: With 100 search steps ThoughtSculpt (MCTS) with GPT-4 reaches 66.0 word / 83.0 letter / 35.0 game success, above ToT's reported 60 / 78 / 20; with 20 steps it already matches ToT at 100.
results.table: Table 8, row THOUGHTSCULPT (MCTS) (100 search steps), column % word

results.claim: On CommonGen-Hard with GPT-3.5, both ThoughtSculpt variants far exceed ToT coverage; DFS is slightly higher than MCTS on coverage.
results.quote: While THOUGHTSCULPT with DFS achieves the highest coverage of 79.6% (GPT-3.5) and 99.1% (GPT-4)
results.note: MCTS gets 77.9 (GPT-3.5) and 99.0 (GPT-4); with GPT-4 gaps are tiny (CoT 96.1, Self-refine 98.5, ToT 98.8)

results.claim: GPT-4 preference judging of coverage plus appropriateness favours MCTS over DFS on Constrained Generation.
results.setup: Constrained Generation, both base LMs, GPT-4 as judge; values only shown in Figure 6 bars, not in text

results.claim: MCTS costs about 2.2x the ToT cost per case on story outline with GPT-4, and 1.6x on crossword.
results.setup: Story Outline Improvement, gpt-4-0125-preview; 25.0k input / 9.9k output tokens for MCTS
results.table: Table 4, row THOUGHTSCULPT with MCTS, column Cost per case
results.note: Main text says MCTS needs 1.2x more computation than ToT; token counts in Table 4 (25.0k/9.9k vs 10.1k/4.9k) imply a larger ratio. Crossword MCTS $1.491 vs ToT $0.912 (Table 5); CommonGen MCTS $0.217 vs ToT $0.104 (Table 6)

results.claim: Human annotators prefer ThoughtSculpt (MCTS) outlines to ToT and Self-Refine outlines.
results.setup: GPT-3.5 base, Prolific annotators; numeric proportions only in Figure 3

results.claim: On Game of 24, ThoughtSculpt (MCTS, b=5) with a general prompt scores 79 vs ToT (b=5) 74 reported by Yao et al.
results.setup: Game of 24, test set of Yao et al. (2023a); baselines copied from that paper, so base model and prompts differ
results.note: Baseline numbers are reported (Yao et al.), not rerun

results.claim: Weakening both evaluator and generator to Llama3.1-8B-Instruct drops coverage from 99.0 to 90.7; weakening the evaluator alone costs more (96.3) than weakening the generator alone (98.5).
results.setup: Constrained Generation, GPT-4 replaced by Llama3.1-8B-Instruct for the named module(s)
results.quote: These results highlight the critical role of a strong evaluator in deep reasoning tasks

results.claim: Only MCTS shows consistent improvement of interestingness across steps; ToT and Self-refine do not.
results.setup: Story outline, GPT-3.5, Figure 4 (values not in text)

limits: Authors concede that multiple LLM calls cost more than most sampling methods, so it is not advisable where the base LM is already satisfactory.
Evaluation uses a hidden Flan-T5 evaluator trained on GPT-3.5 outlines, which may favour GPT-3.5 outputs; the authors give this as a reason for lower GPT-4 scores.
Small test sets (50 outlines, 20 crossword puzzles); no seeds, variances or significance tests reported.
On CommonGen-Hard, DFS beats MCTS on coverage; MCTS advantage rests on a GPT-4 preference judgment.
Cost claim of 1.2x ToT in the text is lower than the token tables suggest.
Game of 24 baselines are taken from Yao et al. rather than rerun.
Depends on closed OpenAI API models, so exact reproduction can drift; code was promised on publication with no link in the text.
UCB1 constant c and number of rollouts d_rollout are not stated.

terms.definition: gives textual and numerical feedback on a thought node; numeric score serves as the search heuristic and NL feedback conditions the children
produces k candidate child nodes from the task description, current solution and natural language feedback
performs rollouts at deeper layers and backpropagates to update the score of the current decision
holistic evaluates the whole node as a unit; itemized evaluates each sub-unit and returns a list of feedback

code.snippet: UCB1(x) = v(x) + c * sqrt(ln n(x_parent) / n(x))

for j <- 1 to d_rollout: select leaf x by UCB1; expand x into X_child; x <- uniformly_sampled(X_child); for k <- 1 to d_simulation: x <- generate_single_child(x); evaluate reward v(x); propagate v and n back to x0. Return x* with highest reward v.
